NCAAF
MICH @ OHIOST • Sat 12:00pm
MICH +10.5
-112
Spread
Picked: Nov 24 @ 2:02pm
Analysis
Don't argue with me - this is the best rivalry in sports. As bad as Michigan's offense has been this season, Ohio State's defense has been poor over its last four games. Both fanbases are shockingly rooting to lose this game so their respective coaches can be dismissed. Sorry Buckeyes fans, that's not happening. To the Wolverines fans, I expect Kyle Whittingham to be one and done. Even so, expect Michigan's top-10 ranked defense to keep this one close. Ohio State may force the ball to Jeremiah Smith to help clinch him the Heisman Trophy, while I expect Michigan's offense to show some rare signs of life. The Buckeyes win but I promise their fans won't be happy either way. Ohio State 21, Michigan 16.
NCAAF
MICH @ OHIOST • Sat 12:00pm
OHIOST -10.5
-105
Spread
Picked: Nov 26 @ 11:42am
Analysis
I will fade the recency bias I believe is in this line. Ohio State lost last week, but it was also the best offensive performance the team has had since Julian Sayin went down. Luke Fahey played very well. Michigan won, but needed three overtimes to score 18 points. Yes, Michigan's defense can slow down Ohio State, but can Michigan score? I'm skeptical.

On the other side, all the positive momentum the Tar Heels had early this season has disappeared. Now everybody is looking around wondering what exactly the point of all of this was.

2026 NFL playoff picture, standings: 49ers reign over NFC, Jaguars slip in AFC, wild-card battles heat up
A comprehensive look at all seven seeds in the AFC and NFC and the teams on the outside looking in
By
Carter Bahns
Nov 23, 2026
at
11:32 pm ET
9 min read
Getty Images
If there is any truth to the adage that the NFL season does not truly start until Thanksgiving, then now is the time to start taking the playoff race seriously. As the calendar turns to Week 12 and a loaded holiday slate, all seven seeds in both conferences are up for grabs, and there are a number of teams beyond the current cut line that could not only make their way into the bracket but also compete for home-field advantage in the postseason.
Anyone that aims to lock up a first-round bye in the NFC has to get through the San Francisco 49ers, which is a daunting task considering how dominant they appeared on the Week 11 edition of "Sunday Night Football."
And in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars learned a difficult lesson on Sunday about how slim the margins are in the race for the No. 1 seed when they suffered a costly setback against the New York Giants.
With seven weeks of regular-season action to go, here is a snapshot of the playoff picture in both NFL conferences.
AFC standings, playoff picture
Buffalo Bills (9-1)
Denver Broncos (8-2)
Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3)
Cincinnati Bengals (7-3)
Kansas City Chiefs (8-2)
Cleveland Browns (6-4)
Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4)
1. Buffalo Bills (9-1)
Remaining schedule: vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers, vs. Bears, at Broncos, at Dolphins, vs. Jets
The only blemish on the Bills' resume is a three-point divisional loss to the Patriots, but that should not come back to bite them in the AFC East race as they hold a commanding four-game lead. It does make them vulnerable in the battle for the conference's No. 1 seed, though. The schedule is about to stiffen up following a four-game stretch in which Josh Allen feasted on beleaguered opponents and the defense corrected its early-season woes by allowing no more than 12 points in any of those contests.
2. Denver Broncos (8-2)
Remaining schedule: at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers
That the Broncos fended off Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders was critical for Denver's chances of winning the AFC West. Sean Payton's squad holds a tiebreaker over the Chiefs thanks to their higher win percentage against common opponents. It was a rare win by double digits for a team that is prolific at squeaking out victories by a one-score margin and increased the win streak to six games, which is tied for the longest in the conference.
3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3)
Remaining schedule: vs. Titans, at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans, at Cowboys, vs. Commanders, at Colts
Trevor Lawrence endured uncharacteristic struggles in a loss to the Giants that halted the Jaguars' momentum. In each of their previous four games, they scored at least 31 points. They managed only 18 against New York. The AFC South is still theirs by a three-game margin, so the defeat only has implications for seeding inside the top four. This team went all-in at the trade deadline and would thus figure to be disappointed with anything less than the No. 1 seed, but so long as everything comes together in the postseason, one loss in Week 11 will not haunt them.
4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3)
Remaining schedule: vs. Saints, at Browns, vs. Chiefs, at Panthers, at Colts, vs. Ravens, vs. Browns
Monday's last-second loss to the Commanders did not drop the Bengals out of first place in the AFC North, but they slipped behind the Jaguars on a tiebreaker after their head-to-head defeat earlier in the season. Cincinnati is fortunate that none of the other teams in its division picked up a win in Week 11.
5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2)
Remaining schedule: at Bills, at Rams, at Bengals, vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, at Chargers, vs. Raiders
The battle with the Broncos to secure home-field advantage in the Wild Card round could come down to the last week of the season. The Chiefs have done nearly everything they can to lock up one of those prized seeds yet find themselves on the outside looking in due to Denver's tiebreaker in the division. Kansas City has been mauling overmatched opponents of late and needs that to translate to the much stiffer competition that lies ahead over the next five weeks.
6. Cleveland Browns (6-4)
Remaining schedule: vs. Raiders, vs. Bengals, vs. Falcons, at Giants, at Ravens, vs. Colts, at Bengals
The Browns hold a tiebreaker over the Steelers for the No. 6 seed because of their divisional win percentage. They split the regular-season series with Pittsburgh and won their only other AFC North contest, 13-10, over the Baltimore Ravens. Among the more pleasant surprises of the entire NFL season is what first-year coach Todd Monken continues to achieve in turning Deshaun Watson back into a serviceable starting quarterback and how defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg constructed a competitive group following the offseason Myles Garrett trade.
7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4)
Remaining schedule: vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, at Jaguars, vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, at Titans, at Ravens
It was only three weeks ago that the Steelers held sole possession of the AFC North lead. Everything since then has been a disaster. They no-showed a week ago in a primetime loss to the Bengals and, on Sunday, were on the wrong side of the Eagles, who snapped a seven-game losing streak. Tennessee, the Chargers and Miami lead the race for the top selection at 1-9, while the Jets hold three picks in the top 15 thanks to blockbuster trades
By
Josh Edwards
Nov 23, 2026
at
8:09 am ET
5 min read
Getty Images
With the majority of Week 11 in the books, the NFL playoff picture is beginning to take shape. While several teams remain in the thick of the postseason race, others are already looking ahead to the offseason and the opportunity to improve their rosters through the 2027 NFL Draft. Where does each team currently stand in the first-round draft order, and which positions could they look to address? Those answers and more can be found below.
As a reminder, five teams -- Green Bay, Indianapolis, Jacksonville, Chicago and the Los Angeles Rams -- do not own a first-round pick in 2027 due to trades, including the Micah Parsons, Sauce Gardner, Jeffery Simmons, Jordan Davis and Myles Garrett deals.

Tarik Skubal is going to be a New York Met. The two-time Cy Young winner is joining the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million contract that will keep him in Flushing through 2035. That contract breaks the record for both total value and AAV for a pitcher (excluding Shohei Ohtani).
A pre-Thanksgiving frenzy, meanwhile, landed starters Trevor Rogers and Hiromi Itoh, as well as NPB slugger Teruaki Sato, with the Cubs, ALCS MVP Freddy Peralta with the Orioles and Kaima Taira with the Blue Jays. Now, the rest of the free agent class, including solid options like Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Luis Arraez, are racing against the clock before the expected lockout after the CBA expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1.

College football schedule 2026: What to watch in Week 13, TV channels, streaming, Saturday kickoff times
Will Saturday's rivalry games create last-minute madness in the College Football Playoff race?
By
Austin Nivison
Nov 27, 2026
at
12:38 pm ET
4 min read
Getty Images
The final week of college football's regular season is upon us, and this sport has a tendency to save the best for last. It's a week full of rivalry games, and although throwing out the record books is a cliché, it often proves to be the correct approach..
As always, Ohio State and Michigan will meet in The Game, and it's a great example of why college football will be fine with an expanded College Football Playoff. Neither of these teams has hope of getting there, but does that matter to the fan bases? Absolutely not. Neither side wants to lose, and the coach who does is going to get raked over the coals.
Later in the afternoon, there is a game that has big-time implications for the CFP and the Big Ten Championship Game. No. 15 USC and No. 9 UCLA will go head-to-head with both teams alive for a conference championship berth. It's the biggest matchup this rivalry series has seen in more than 20 years.
Tracking FBS conference championship scenarios: Big Ten still unsettled entering Week 13
Austin Nivison
Throughout the day, college football's most storied rivalries will write another chapter. Auburn will try to deal No. 6  Alabama's playoff seeding a major blow in the Iron Bowl, No. 24  Washington will try to keep No. 12  Oregon out of the CFP field and Louisville can send  Kentucky out on a four-game losing streak.
With so much football on throughout the day, we've created a handy guide to help you prioritize your viewing.
All times ET
The best games
Michigan at No. 21 Ohio State -- 12 p.m. on Fox, Fubo (try for free): There may not be major national implications for this edition of The Game — although the Buckeyes have a minuscule shot at reaching the Big Ten title game — but the stakes are still high. Kyle Whittingham is on the hot seat, but what if he finishes the season with a win over No. 4 UCLA and No. 21 Ohio State. On the other side, Ryan Day has already received plenty of criticism throughout this four-loss campaign, but that would reach another level if he lost to this Wolverines squad.
No. 19 Louisville at Kentucky -- 12 p.m. on ESPN2,  Fubo  (try for free): After entering the month of November at 7-1, Kentucky is just trying to avoid an 0-4 collapse at the end of the regular season. In order to do that, the Wildcats will have to beat rival Louisville, which also just happens to be coach Will Stein's alma mater. This season has been a slight disappointment for the Cardinals, who hoped to be in the playoff conversation at this stage, but beating Kentucky and reaching nine wins would be a great way to go out on a high note.
Duke at No. 8 Wake Forest -- 3:30 p.m. on ESPN,  Fubo (try for free): Wake Forest has to be in contention for one of the most doubted College Football Playoff contenders since the format was adopted in 2014. The Demon Deacons don't have a roster full of blue-chip prospects or high-profile transfers, but they still crush opponents every weekend anyway. The final test of the regular season for Jake Dickert's squad is a plucky Duke team. The Blue Devils are coming off a bad loss to Clemson, but they're capable of hanging with just about anyone in the ACC.
No. 15 USC at No. 9 UCLA -- 3:30 p.m. on CBS, CBSSports.com, Paramount+ Premium : The Bruins are looking to avoid becoming the first Big Ten team in conference history to lose two straight games after starting the season 10-0. The rival Trojans would love to assist them in making history, and they're a road favorite in the Rose Bowl. The uncertainty surrounding UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach certainly plays a factor in that, but the offense hasn't always looked great even with Dieffenbach in the game. The Bruins defense will have to make USC quarterback Jayden Maiava uncomfortable for 60 minutes Saturday.
Auburn at No. 6 Alabama -- 7:30 p.m. on ABC,  Fubo (try for free): It's been 16 years since Auburn last beat Alabama in Tuscaloosa, and that win required a heroic effort from Cam Newton. Auburn quarterback  Byrum Brown has played relatively well for the Tigers this season, but he hasn't exactly been Newton. The Crimson Tide certainly hope Brown doesn't pull any of that magic out of his sleeve because a home loss in the Iron Bowl would put a big dent in Alabama's College Football Playoff ranking. Despite a two-touchdown spread, this game can get sideways, as we've seen plenty of times in the 21st century.
No. 24 Washington at No. 12 Oregon -- 7:30 p.m. on NBC,  Fubo (try for free): The Ducks are probably the one team that no national championship contender wants to see in the College Football Playoff. After a 4-3 start, Oregon has won four in a row and can still reach the Big Ten title game and the playoff. The only thing standing between the Ducks and their goals is a Washington team that has won four of its last five games to sneak inside the CFP rankings. Are the Huskies capable of going into Autzen Stadium and effectively ending their rival's season? I guess we're about to find out.

One week ago, UCLA was 10-0 and seemingly cruising to a spot in the Big Ten Championship and a berth in the College Football Playoff.
Now, the No. 9 Bruins have a loss, their CFP hopes are dwindling, and they're underdogs against rival USC in the final game of the regular season. But the path is clear: Win, and they're in both the Big Ten Championship and likely the playoff. But can they do it as a one-touchdown underdog with potentially the third-string quarterback leading the offense?
We'll find out this final weekend of the regular season, when rivalries can throw everything out of sorts.
The biggest games are in the Big Ten, where the championship race still involves six teams, but the roads could run through Eugene, Oregon, and Iowa City. No. 12 Oregon hosts No. 24 Washington after No. 13 Iowa knocked off No. 25 Nebraska on Friday.
The Hawkeyes have five different ways into the Big Ten title game (all require a win), and Oregon has eight possibilities, including four with a loss. Only UCLA controls its own destiny with a win.
Yeah, it's wild.
So, read up on the conference tiebreakers and check out our experts' picks for the biggest games in the final week of the regular season.
No. 21 Ohio State vs. Michigan
Saturday -- Noon on Fox,  Fubo (try free): While Michigan's offense is among the worst in college football, the Wolverines can play some defense. Only two teams have surpassed 300 yards of offense against Michigan this season. It's no certainty that an Ohio State offense operating with backup quarterback Luke Fahey will be able to move the football. If Michigan is able to run the football against an Ohio State defense that hasn't been at its best recently, it can run some clock and keep the football out of the Buckeyes' hands. Mix it all up, and you get a low-scoring, grimy rivalry game. Ohio State has the game's top playmaker in Jeremiah Smith, and he'll make a game-changing play at some point to help the Buckeyes win. But the Wolverines have enough defensive strength to keep it close. Pick: Michigan +10.5 -- David Cobb

Fan shoves Luka Dončić after he flings his wristband at a woman in crowd
This is not a good look for Luka, regardless of his innocent explanation
By
Brad Botkin
Nov 28, 2026
at
2:03 am ET
2 min read
Getty Images
The Los Angeles Lakers blew a 20-point lead in a loss to the San Antonio Spurs on Friday, and Luka Dončić was not happy about it. Not only was this a gut-punch loss in a game for early dibs on the West's No. 1 seed, but Dončić has been ice cold from 3 over the last two-plus weeks (26 for 100) and it continued in San Antonio with a 1-for-13 showing.
This was at least the surface context under which a clearly frustrated Dončić walked off the court, and as he made his way toward the locker room, he flung his wristband at a woman in the crowd. Moments later, Dončić turned around and went to retrieve the wristband, at which point the man who was with the woman handed it back to him and then shoved the Lakers superstar before multiple security guards quickly intervened.
A fan shoved Luka after he threw his band toward them 😳 pic.twitter.com/AKh93Z9QUK— NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 28, 2026
"I just threw my wristband, like I do almost every game," Dončić explained. "Then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it and then he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else."
The reporter asked if the fan had said anything to Dončić that perhaps instigated the wristband fling, or if there were words after the shove (which there pretty clearly were), but Dončić stuck to his innocent explanation of what appeared to be a pretty aggressive act on his part.
Luka Dončić was asked about the fan shoving him after the game. He said that he tossed his wrist band to a fan and then heard them say they don't want it, so he returned to get it and then got shoved. pic.twitter.com/7mBjXKWbAD— Jared Weiss (@JaredWeissNBA) November 28, 2026
If you watch the video again, you can pretty clearly see the woman saying something to Dončić before he flings the wristband. Maybe she was trash-talking him. Or, maybe she was responding to the middle finger that Dončić appeared to flip toward the crowd moments before.
Cameras caught Luka Dončić FLIPPING OFF and then casually tossing his wristband at an older female Spurs fan. He then walked back to snatch it away.
That is when the fan’s angry husband stepped in and shoved him. 👀 https://t.co/aKESpD7Qnm pic.twitter.com/eZpioMSyqe— SpursRΞPORTΞR (@SpursReporter) November 28, 2026
Either way, this is not a good look for Dončić. That was not a fan-friendly wristband giveaway, as Dončić wants you to believe. That is a back-turned slingshot at an elderly woman. If that's how he hands out wristbands after games (heaven forbid to a little kid), by slinging it into their chest as he keeps right on walking by, he's got some real growing up to do.
Even if these people were taunting Dončić, he can't do that. We'll see if any further explanation as to what was said in this exchange surfaces, but at first glance this looks like Dončić, for whatever reason, firing a wristband in frustration at a woman, and a man next to her taking offense to that aggression, hence the shove.
This definitely feels like an incident the league is going to have to address.

Aaron Rodgers claims he was 'barred' from Steelers' facility: Why QB went scorched earth on Mike McCarthy
Here's why the QB went scorched earth on Mike McCarthy
By
John Breech
Nov 27, 2026
at
7:15 pm ET
2 min read
Imagn Images
Based on how they played Friday, it seems like the Pittsburgh Steelers have already put the Aaron Rodgers drama behind them, but the same can't be said for the four-time NFL MVP.
Rodgers has taken some heat this week for breaking the sanctity of the locker room and he decided to respond to that accusation by sending a text message to Al Michaels, who was on the call for Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Broncos.
During the fourth quarter of the Amazon Prime stream, Michaels read out loud what Rodgers had sent him.
"A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room," Michaels said of what Rodgers wrote. "The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That's why I went to [Pat] McAfee."
It's a short text, but there's a lot to unpack here.
For one, let's start with the fact Rodgers claims he was "barred'' from the team facility. The Steelers announced Rodgers' benching at 11:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday and they did that even though no one in the organization had actually spoken to Rodgers before the announcement came out (They did speak with his agent, though).
Steelers coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Rodgers after the QB gave him an ultimatum at some point on Tuesday: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. Although Rodgers didn't get released at that point, that did lead to his benching.
The QB didn't show up for practice on Wednesday, and according to multiple reports, that was because the team had excused him from practice, but according to Rodgers, it was because he was banned from the facility.
The Steelers' decision to lock Rodgers out is why he ultimately chose  to talk to Pat McAfee on Wednesday. The interview was a wild ride, with Rodgers throwing out multiple accusations at Mike McCarthy, including that he had missed meetings, fallen asleep during meetings and skipped walk-throughs.
Just hours after the interview with McAfee ended, Rodgers was released.
During Thursday's slate of Thanksgiving games, Rodgers was called out by Tom Brady for breaking the "sanctity" of the NFL locker room, and an accusation like that from Brady likely rubbed Rodgers the wrong way, which would explain why he used Brady's wording in his text to Michaels.
Based on Rodgers' claim, he may not have done the McAfee interview if he hadn't been barred from the facility, and if there had been no interview, this situation might have turned out differently. But it also seems Rodgers was determined to burn every bridge on his way out of town, so it's hard to say whether things would have turned out differently.
Either way, the Steelers have moved on from the former quarterback and they did so in dominant fashion by beating the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Friday.

How Mark Pope's inexplicable overtime coaching blunders doomed Kentucky in rock-bottom loss to Wichita State
Two baffling tactical miscues in the final 35 seconds of overtime capped an inexcusable collapse and pushed the Wildcats coach onto a scalding hot seat
By
David Cobb
Nov 28, 2026
at
12:58 am ET
3 min read
Mark Pope's Kentucky tenure hit rock bottom on Friday night as the Wildcats suffered from coaching malpractice in the final minute of a 73-71 overtime home loss to Wichita State. The defeat dropped UK to 4-3 and 0-3 against teams ranked inside the top 100 at KenPom.
While Kentucky's relinquishing of a 14-point lead to an AAC foe spoke to the program's overall downward trend, the final possessions of overtime underscored the extent to which in-game coaching is an issue for the Wildcats.
When Kentucky committed a dead-ball turnover with 34.2 seconds left while trailing 73-71 in the extra period, the Wildcats opted against fouling immediately. Instead, they attempted to force a turnover in the backcourt. But when Wichita State broke the press, Kentucky still didn't foul, despite there being only a 4-second difference between the shot clock and game clock.
Mark Pope buyout, contract details: How much it would cost Kentucky to fire coach after loss to Wichita State
Cameron Salerno
The Shockers offered Pope a potential bailout with 5.1 seconds left when Jahari Long's pass in the lane trickled out of bounds under the basket. But after letting Wichita State use virtually the entire shot clock, the Wildcats still needed to go the length of the court in warp speed in order to get a game-tying or go-ahead look.
That's when Pope made an even more egregious coaching blunder.
Play called by Pope wasn't legal
After the teams called dueling timeouts, which gave Pope plenty of time to strategize, UK attempted to run an impermissible inbounds play. Sophomore guard Alex Wilkins was the inbounds passer. But instead of passing it to another inbounds player, he passed it to freshman guard Mason Williams, who was also out of bounds.
The idea was to misdirect the Wichita State defense and allow Wilkins to then receive a pass from Williams with a running start. The only problem is that it wasn't allowed.
Had the inbounds play occurred after a made basket in a live-ball situation, the pass would have been allowed. But since Wichita State had committed a turnover, the Wildcats couldn't pass the ball to an out-of-bounds player (or run the baseline). It was a dead-ball situation.
I think this might be rock bottom for Mark Pope pic.twitter.com/vzhSV2ybG2— Clay Fink (@clay_fink) November 28, 2026
Either Pope did not know the rule or forgot the situation. Whichever it was, it was an inexcusable miscue for 12th-year head coach.
"That's 100% on me, guys," Pope said after the game. "That is 100% me. Somehow, that changed to a live ball in my mind, and I messed that up. Really costly. It's a tough one to carry as a coach, for sure."
Even still, the Wildcats forced a Wichita State turnover on the subsequent play and managed to get a clean look at a potential go-ahead 3-pointer for sharpshooter Milan Momcilovic just before the buzzer.
But when his attempt clanged off the rim, the horn sounded on a loss that will be hard for Pope to recover from.
Getting out-rebounded 55-36 by Wichita State was one thing. Perhaps in a winning effort, Pope could have written that off as a byproduct of star center Malachi Moreno's absence as he missed the game due to concussion protocol.
Mark Pope says the out of bounds gaffe was “100% on me”: pic.twitter.com/olXHeY2bTO— Kevin Sweeney (@CBB_Central) November 28, 2026
Squeaking out an uncomfortably close win against a quality mid-major foe without Moreno would have done nothing to alleviate the pressure mounting on Pope. But it would have bought him more time to plug the glaring number of holes on Kentucky's ship heading into a December that includes games against No. 2 Virginia (Dec. 2), No. 25 Louisville (Dec. 12) and North Carolina in the CBS Sports Classic (Dec. 19).
But with the final minute of overtime being defined by two inexplicable coaching blunders that led directly to a loss, Pope's hot seat is going from hot to scalding just seven games into the season.
Pope also to blame for lack of talent
It's been clear since an 89-69 loss to Kansas on Nov. 10 that UK's roster is ill-equipped to compete at the highest levels of college basketball. That's on Pope, too.
But the former title-winning Kentucky forward dug the Wildcats out of an early hole last season and coaxed them to the second round of the NCAA Tournament.
This time around, it's getting harder to envision Pope getting these Wildcats anywhere close to where the program expects to be. UK landed on the outside looking in of Friday's 76-team CBS Sports Bracketology update.
Mark Pope Boo’d out of Rupp Arena pic.twitter.com/C4n2tEvQ0z— Bleed Blue Network (@BleedBNetwork) November 28, 2026
After the loss, Kentucky is now 66th at KenPom. Even amid last season's struggles, Kentucky never fell below 33rd at its worst.
Pope may have been talking specifically about the botched overtime inbounds play when he said that it's "100% on me," but at this point, it's hard to argue that the same statement doesn't apply to the status of Kentucky's basketball program as a whole.
